meta.name: narrative-jev-control-set-v0
meta.purpose: Design 2026-10-29 §9 step 7 / D10: narrative claims (zh-TW KOL paraphrases) against verbatim official excerpts. narrative_apply stays off until every case the owner labels says_nothing gets no supports and no contradicts from JEV. Labels are evaluation metadata and are never sent to the model.
meta.labeler: owner labels recorded 2026-10-29 (label_source owner-2026-10-29); expected_label equals owner_label, which jev_eval_control_set.py scores against
meta.excerpt_rule: source.text is a raw verbatim substring of the source file (no whitespace canonicalisation); locator = 1-based line range; text_sha256 = sha256 of source.text
meta.symbol_rule: symbol = the run symbol narrative_apply would pass for the theme-scope revision (cfg symbols joined by ',')

meta.label_policy_v1: v1 (gold set 2026-10-21): period or entity conflict = contradicts; mixed clauses = says_nothing, tagged mixed; unit scaling = supports
meta.label_policy_rule: v1 still holds, except for narrative checks: when the official statement covers a shorter or different period than the narrative claim, the label is says_nothing; contradicts only when the official text explicitly states the opposite for the same period. Stage mismatches (sampling vs volume production, a goal vs the current state) are says_nothing.

cases.claim: 客戶為保出貨量主動壓低每台伺服器的記憶體用量

source.text:
We expect server unit growth in the high-teens percentage range in both calendar 2026 and 2027. This
strong server unit growth is supported by a modestly lower rate of content growth than prior
expectations, amid tight memory supply. Growing model parameter size, longer context lengths and
higher concurrency continue to increase the memory and storage content required to execute AI
workloads efficiently.

cases.note: 原文只說內容成長率略低於預期、背景是供給吃緊；沒有說客戶主動壓低，也沒說是為了保出貨（§7.3 預期）

In NAND, for calendar 2026, we expect industry bit shipments to grow in the low-20s percentage range,
slightly above our prior expectations. We expect Micron NAND supply to grow less than industry supply
growth in calendar 2026. For calendar 2027 and 2028, we expect industry NAND bit shipments to grow
approximately in the mid-20s percentage range and the industry to remain supply constrained in both
years.

In DRAM, for calendar 2026, we expect industry bit shipments to grow in the mid-20s percentage range.
We expect Micron DRAM supply to grow approximately in line with industry supply growth. For calendar
2027 and 2028, we expect industry DRAM bit shipments to grow approximately in the low-20s percentage
range and the industry to remain supply constrained in both years. We expect industry HBM bit shipments
to grow faster than conventional DRAM through calendar 2028.

The structural gap between DRAM supply and demand growth rates is resulting in ongoing supply
tightness, and cleanroom additions are required to augment node-transition supply growth and help
narrow the gap. Even with additional industry DRAM cleanroom space plans, with robust demand trends
including new upside requests from customers, we do not have line of sight to when supply and demand
will return to balance.
